text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] geo-dns resolver anomalies detected — elevated NXDOMAIN/timeout rates from EU edge resolvers (eu-west-1) affecting name lookups for model endpoints. Automatic retry fallback triggered.

Jordan (oncall): saw this at 08:04 UTC, paging in. i'm on it. can someone grab recent customer error rates? :eyes:

Alex P: grabbing metrics — 08:05 checks: token-generate 5xx rate up from 0.1% to ~1.9% for eu-west by 08:03; median latency for name resolution increased to 620ms for a subset of requests. traffic still routed but lots of resolver timeouts -> retries.

Maya R: are we sure it's external resolver (cloudflare/route53) and not our edge caching? i've hit a couple dig timeouts from our eu test runner.

Nina - EngSRE: quick sanity: ran `dig @1.1.1.1 model-eu.redwood.internal +time=2 +tries=1` and got repeated SERVFAIL/NXDOMAINs for some subdomains. dig to AWS resolver (169.254.x) returns answers. suggests upstream CF/Route53 path issues.

Alex P: paste of sample output:```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api-eu.redwood.com +short
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```

Jordan (oncall): moving to mitigation plan from runbook 3b: 1) short TTL change on critical geo records to 60s, 2) enable internal-resolver-forwarding fallback, 3) open support tickets with Cloudflare + AWS Route53. executing steps now.

Maya R: i'll prep support ticket with packet captures and EDNS traces. Ping Cloudflare status too.

support-runbook-bot: runbook 3b acknowledged. estimated customer impact: partial degradation for EU edge only, estimated 1-3% request failures, some clients may see retries and higher latency. Follow escalation matrix if >5% or >20min no improvement.

Jordan (oncall): changing TTL on geo dns records to 60s via console now (will push to secondary nameservers). applying: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://short-ttl.json --hosted-zone-id ZONE123`

Nina - EngSRE: enabling forwarding: updating edge resolver config to `forwarders: ["169.254.169.253","10.2.4.10"]` and rolling to eu-west edge pool. will push canary to 2 instances first.

Alex P: cloudflare status shows "partial outage in EU region" — I'll attach link: https://cloudflarestatus.example/incident/abcd. opening ticket ID CF-2026-1123.

Maya R: contacted AWS support for Route53 logs/queries spike — ticket AWS-98765 opened. attaching dig/traceroute results.

Jordan (oncall): can someone validate client-facing errors dropping? nina, after canary roll, run synthetic checks.

Nina - EngSRE: canary roll -> done on 2 nodes at 08:11. synthetic checks: initial improvement — resolution times down to ~45ms from those canaries. escalating to full roll at 08:13.

Alex P: metrics at 08:15 show 5xx down to 0.6%, latency median down to 180ms. still some unresolved sources but trending good.

Maya R: reminder: reduce cache TTL in our intermediate proxies too so clients pick new records quickly. I'll push a 60s cache policy to frontline proxies.

Jordan (oncall): notification to support & ops: `@support` notice — we've applied internal fallback + reduced TTLs; tracking Cloudflare/AWS tickets. Customer impact: partial failures mostly mitigated; continue monitoring.

incident-bot: Created incident page: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-042 (owner: Jordan).

Alex P: Cloudflare replied: investigating BGP flap causing intermittent resolver blackholing for specific POPs; they recommend using our secondary authoritative nameservers as short-term.

Jordan (oncall): decision: programmatic geo policy tweak to prefer secondary NS set for eu-west until CF resolves. applying now (will not change records, only ns priority in our geo-rules).

Nina - EngSRE: change applied at 08:22. performing full sweep synthetics. initial sweep shows global resolution success >= 99.7%.

Maya R: customer impacted set: 47 customer accounts showed retry errors; support team notified with list + suggested mitigation steps (retry/backoff).

Jordan (oncall): contacting account execs for top 5 affected customers. ops to draft status update for status.redwood.com.

Alex P: heap of Cloudflare logs attached to CF ticket, they acknowledge route flap and are pushing fix. AWS says no anomalies on Route53 side.

support-runbook-bot: escalation threshold cleared (<2% impact sustained). continue 1hr observation window per runbook.

Nina - EngSRE: monitoring continues. i'll leave the forwarding fallback in place for 30m post-stable, then slowly revert tests.

Jordan (oncall): logged mitigation steps in incident doc and added timeline. i'd like a postmortem if CF confirms root cause. assigning to Maya for liaison + notes.

Maya R: will own postmortem coordination and write initial draft. will include: timeline, mitigation actions, customer comms, and follow-ups (improve automatic failover to secondary NS in geo-controller).

Alex P: closing note: we'll automate a synthetic probe to detect resolver SERVFAIL and auto-enable forwarding next week (low-risk deploy).

Jordan (oncall): incident moved to monitoring at 08:33 UTC. will update once tickets close. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident state -> MONITORING.
